representative:
Historically, the process of making software flowed from design to implementation (never mind the fact that some of the greatest software broke this rule).

With agents, it feels more necessary than ever to have a system that permits quick two-way iteration.

We hope the attention to detail in the new Amp TUI will be emblematic of the software you build with it.

Make it work, make it fast, make it 𝒔𝒉𝒊𝒎𝒎𝒆𝒓
A completely rebuilt-from-the-ground Amp TUI is out today!
outlier:
The delight of novel experiences will be shadowed by nostalgia for what we leave behind. It’s normal. Pour one out for the Old Ways, then move on. Figure out the new world. Do things. The New Way is learned through doing.

There will be highs and there will be lows. Great movements are built on emotion, not always positive ones. There will be those who lean into the negative, and the world has no shortage of demagogues who will gladly trade you more cortisol for influence and power over you.

You decide which path you want for yourself. A big part of that is choosing your community. For me, I want to be among those who are leaning into the delight and joy and wonder of it all. Someday, you'll tell your grandkids: I was there when the world changed. And I set my hand to the stone to build the one you’re living in now.

recent_posts.title:
Note on GPT 5.5's data retention requirements, which appear to apply broadly to agents using this model. If you're willing to waive ZDR (zero data retention) by OpenAI, you can use it in Amp with these instructions.

(Still no training on this data, even w/o ZDR, in Amp)
recent_posts.summary: GPT-5.5 has data retention requirements that apply broadly to agents using the model. Users who waive Zero Data Retention (ZDR) with OpenAI can use GPT-5.5 in the Amp coding tool. Even without ZDR, OpenAI does not train on data processed through Amp.

recent_posts.title:
Reminder that Amp has always had and will continue to have usage-based pricing, so you pay for the tokens you use.

It uses frontier models that are best suited for agentic coding (GPT 5.4 for nuanced + long-running tasks and Opus for interactive use + frontend)
recent_posts.summary: Amp uses usage-based pricing where developers pay only for the tokens they consume. It leverages frontier models optimized for agentic coding: GPT for nuanced and long-running tasks, and Claude Opus for interactive use and frontend work.

recent_posts.title: The emotive surface area of voice interaction is so much broader than text. It's a new dimension of "wow" in UX that we've only begun to scratch the surface of.
recent_posts.summary: Voice interaction offers a significantly richer emotional range compared to text-based interfaces, representing an underexplored frontier in UX design. The potential for creating impactful, emotionally resonant user experiences through voice is still largely untapped.

recent_posts.title: We've switched deep mode in Amp over to GPT-5.4. Should be less verbose than stock 5.4 in other settings. I've been using this as my main agent for the past couple weeks or so and it's great.
recent_posts.summary: Amp has switched its deep mode to GPT-5.4, tuned to be less verbose than the default GPT-5.4 configuration. The author has been using it as their primary coding agent for a couple of weeks and reports positive results.

top_posts.title:
Historically, the process of making software flowed from design to implementation (never mind the fact that some of the greatest software broke this rule).

With agents, it feels more necessary than ever to have a system that permits quick two-way iteration.
top_posts.summary: Traditional software development followed a linear design-to-implementation flow, but AI agents are changing this dynamic. The shift toward agentic development makes rapid two-way iteration between design and implementation increasingly essential rather than optional.
